title: Signed completed integral Tate lines are bounded constructible and derived complete
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite-dimensional extension of Q_l, W a scheme on which l is invertible, D an auxiliary finite-field datum with l different from D.p, and m an integer. Form the signed completed root line integralCoefficientTwist D l hl E W m in degree zero as in def-coefficient-twists-detailed. This object satisfies boundedConstructibleDerivedCompleteIntegral: its canonical augmented reduction tower is a derived-limit tower and all positive derived reductions are constructible in one common finite cohomological interval. The construction and the predicate are those of def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients and def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed.

source.place: Integral root line, its signed tensor powers and internal duals; the existing integralCoefficientTwist_constructible declaration in Sheaf.Paper.CoefficientTwistsDetailed.

proof.text: The existing pur_twist_sheaf_locally_free theorem gives rank one for the completed first root line. Apply the rank field of OrdinaryLineScalar.exists_lineData to obtain rank one for every signed tensor power. Integer cases identify its generic signedLinePower with the published coefficientTwistLine, including exponent zero and internal duals at negative exponents.

Apply completedLine_derived to this rank-one completed line. Its second clause gives completeness for the actual augmented integral reduction tower; its first clause identifies each derived reduction with the degree-zero single of ordinary change of rings along the actual completed coefficient projection.

Use scalarExtensionDual_localIsomorphism to see that each ordinary reduction is still invertible, hence rank one. The generic finiteLocallyFreeLine_models theorem over the positive finite quotient ring gives constructibility of this sheaf. This argument needs no identification with a separately constructed finite Tate line.

Apply constructible_single_support using the canonical derived-reduction isomorphism from the second step. It gives finite cohomological support, constructible homology in every degree, and support contained in {0}. These are exactly intrinsic finite-torsion constructibility and the common interval [0,0]. Pair these with completeness to prove the unchanged integral predicate. The empty scheme has empty support, so the same interval works there too.

proof_origin.place: Signed tensor powers and duals of the integral root line; reuse the existing general completed-line and finite-line theorems, with the same [0,0] interval.
